Runtime
=======

System-related functionality, process management, and observability.

Eg [`Deno.mainModule`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.mainModule)
, [`Deno.exit`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.exit)
, [`Deno.cwd`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.cwd)

---------

f

Registers the given function as a listener of the given signal event.

Returns the path to the current deno executable.

[Deno.hostname](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.hostname "Deno.hostname")

Get the `hostname` of the machine the Deno process is running on.

f

[Deno.loadavg](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.loadavg "Deno.loadavg")

Returns an array containing the 1, 5, and 15 minute load averages. The load average is a measure of CPU and IO utilization of the last one, five, and 15 minute periods expressed as a fractional number. Zero means there is no load. On Windows, the three values are always the same and represent the current load, not the 1, 5 and 15 minute load averages.

f

Returns an object describing the memory usage of the Deno process and the V8 subsystem measured in bytes.

f

Returns the release version of the Operating System.

f

[Deno.osUptime](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.osUptime "Deno.osUptime")

Returns the Operating System uptime in number of seconds.

f

[Deno.refTimer](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.refTimer "Deno.refTimer")

Make the timer of the given `id` block the event loop from finishing.

f

[Deno.removeSignalListener](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.removeSignalListener "Deno.removeSignalListener")

Removes the given signal listener that has been registered with [`Deno.addSignalListener`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.addSignalListener)
.

f

[Deno.systemMemoryInfo](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.systemMemoryInfo "Deno.systemMemoryInfo")

Displays the total amount of free and used physical and swap memory in the system, as well as the buffers and caches used by the kernel.

f

Returns the user id of the process on POSIX platforms. Returns null on Windows.

f

Make the timer of the given `id` not block the event loop from finishing.

function [Deno.addSignalListener](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener.function_addSignalListener_0) addSignalListener(  signal: [Signal](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Signal) ,  handler: () => void,  ): void`

Registers the given function as a listener of the given signal event.

    Deno.addSignalListener(
      "SIGTERM",
      () => {
        console.log("SIGTERM!")
      }
    );
    

_Note_: On Windows only `"SIGINT"` (CTRL+C), `"SIGBREAK"` (CTRL+Break), `"SIGTERM"`, `"SIGQUIT"`, `"SIGHUP"`, and `"SIGWINCH"` are supported.

### Parameters [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener.parameters)

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener.function_addsignallistener_0_parameter_signal) signal: [Signal](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Signal) `

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener.function_addsignallistener_0_parameter_handler) handler: () => void`

### Return Type [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.addSignalListener.return-type)

`void`

function [Deno.chdir](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.chdir)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

allow-read

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.chdir.function_chdir_0) chdir(directory: string | URL): void`

Change the current working directory to the specified path.

    Deno.chdir("/home/userA");
    Deno.chdir("../userB");
    Deno.chdir("C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Java");
    

Throws [`Deno.errors.NotFound`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/errors/#Deno.errors.NotFound)
 if directory not found.

Throws [`Deno.errors.PermissionDenied`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/errors/#Deno.errors.PermissionDenied)
 if the user does not have operating system file access rights.

Requires `allow-read` permission.

### Parameters [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.chdir.parameters)

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.chdir.function_chdir_0_parameter_directory) directory: string | URL`

### Return Type [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.chdir.return-type)

`void`

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.cwd.function_cwd_0) cwd(): string`

Return a string representing the current working directory.

If the current directory can be reached via multiple paths (due to symbolic links), `cwd()` may return any one of them.

function [Deno.exit](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.exit)

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.exit.function_exit_0) exit(code?: number): never`

Exit the Deno process with optional exit code.

If no exit code is supplied then Deno will exit with return code of `0`.

In worker contexts this closes the current worker using Deno's internal worker close operation. It does not call the current `self.close` property.

    Deno.exit(5);
    

### Parameters [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.exit.parameters)

optional

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.loadavg.function_loadavg_0) loadavg(): number[]`

Returns an array containing the 1, 5, and 15 minute load averages. The load average is a measure of CPU and IO utilization of the last one, five, and 15 minute periods expressed as a fractional number. Zero means there is no load. On Windows, the three values are always the same and represent the current load, not the 1, 5 and 15 minute load averages.

    console.log(Deno.loadavg());  // e.g. [ 0.71, 0.44, 0.44 ]
    

Requires `allow-sys` permission.

On Windows there is no API available to retrieve this information and this method returns `[ 0, 0, 0 ]`.

Removes the given signal listener that has been registered with [`Deno.addSignalListener`](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.addSignalListener)

    const listener = () => {

interface [Deno.Env](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env)

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

allow-env

An interface containing methods to interact with the process environment variables.

Environment variables can also be loaded from a `.env` file by using the `--env-file` flag when running a Deno program:

    deno run --env-file=.env --allow-env main.ts
    

If `--env-file` is specified without a value, it defaults to loading `.env` from the current working directory:

    deno run --env-file --allow-env main.ts
    

Learn more at [the Deno docs](https://docs.deno.com/runtime/reference/env_variables/)
.

### Methods [#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.methods)

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.method_get_0) [get](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Env) (key: string): string | undefined`

Retrieve the value of an environment variable.

Returns `undefined` if the supplied environment variable is not defined.

    console.log(Deno.env.get("HOME"));  // e.g. outputs "/home/alice"
    console.log(Deno.env.get("MADE_UP_VAR"));  // outputs undefined
    

Requires `allow-env` permission.

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.method_set_1) [set](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Env) (  key: string,  value: string,  ): void`

Set the value of an environment variable.

    Deno.env.set("SOME_VAR", "Value");
    Deno.env.get("SOME_VAR");  // outputs "Value"
    

Requires `allow-env` permission.

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.method_delete_2) [delete](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Env) (key: string): void`

Delete the value of an environment variable.

    Deno.env.set("SOME_VAR", "Value");
    Deno.env.delete("SOME_VAR");  // outputs "undefined"
    

Requires `allow-env` permission.

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.method_has_3) [has](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Env) (key: string): boolean`

Check whether an environment variable is present or not.

    Deno.env.set("SOME_VAR", "Value");
    Deno.env.has("SOME_VAR");  // outputs true
    

Requires `allow-env` permission.

`[#](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.Env.method_toobject_4) [toObject](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/runtime/#Deno.Env) (): { [index: string]: string; }`

Returns a snapshot of the environment variables at invocation as a simple object of keys and values.

    Deno.env.set("TEST_VAR", "A");
    const myEnv = Deno.env.toObject();
    console.log(myEnv.SHELL);
    Deno.env.set("TEST_VAR", "B");
    console.log(myEnv.TEST_VAR);  // outputs "A"
    

Requires `allow-env` permission.

Users are discouraged from code branching based on this information, as assumptions about what is available in what build environment might change over time. Developers should specifically sniff out the features they intend to use.

variable [Deno.exitCode](https://docs.deno.com/api/deno/~/Deno.memoryUsage#Deno.exitCode)

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The exit code for the Deno process.

If no exit code has been supplied, then Deno will assume a return code of `0`.

When setting an exit code value, a number or non-NaN string must be provided, otherwise a TypeError will be thrown.

    console.log(Deno.exitCode); //-> 0
    Deno.exitCode = 1;
    console.log(Deno.exitCode); //-> 1
